chapters.title: Visions of God
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 1

1And it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was among the exiles by the river Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.

2On the fifth day of the month, in the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's exile,

3the word of the LORD came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar; and the hand of the LORD was on him there.

The Living Creatures

4I looked: a storm wind was coming out of the north, a great cloud with fire flashing through it and brightness all around it, and from the middle of it, from the middle of the fire, something like the gleam of amber.

5From the middle of it came the likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: they had the likeness of a human.

6Each had four faces, and each of them had four wings.

7Their legs were straight, and the soles of their feet were like the sole of a calf's foot; and they sparkled like the gleam of burnished bronze.

8They had human hands under their wings on their four sides. As for the faces and wings of the four of them,

9their wings touched one another. They did not turn as they went; each went straight ahead.

10As for the likeness of their faces, each of the four had the face of a human, and on the right the face of a lion, and on the left the face of an ox, and each of the four had the face of an eagle.

11Such were their faces. Their wings were spread out above: each had two wings touching those of another, and two covering their bodies.

12Each went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit would go, they went, without turning as they went.

13As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches. Fire moved back and forth among the living creatures; the fire was bright, and lightning went out of the fire.

14The living creatures darted back and forth like the appearance of a flash of lightning.

The Wheels

15As I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground beside each of the living creatures, for each of their four faces.

16The appearance of the wheels and their making was like the gleam of beryl, and all four had one likeness; their appearance and their making were as if a wheel were inside a wheel.

17When they went, they went in any of their four directions, without turning as they went.

18As for their rims, they were high and fearsome, and the rims of all four were full of eyes all around.

19When the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them; and when the living creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose.

20Wherever the spirit would go, they went, wherever the spirit went, and the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.

21When those went, these went; when those stood still, these stood still; and when those rose from the ground, the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.

The Throne

22Over the heads of the living creature was the likeness of an expanse, like the gleam of awe-inspiring crystal, spread out over their heads above.

23Under the expanse their wings were stretched out straight, one toward another. Each had two that covered its body on one side, and each had two that covered it on the other side.

24When they went, I heard the sound of their wings, like the sound of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, a sound of tumult like the sound of an army. When they stood still, they let down their wings.

25A voice came from above the expanse that was over their heads; when they stood still, they let down their wings.

26Above the expanse that was over their heads was something like the appearance of sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne; and on the likeness of the throne, high above it, was a likeness like the appearance of a human.

27I saw something like the gleam of amber, like the appearance of fire enclosed all around, from the appearance of His waist upward; and from the appearance of His waist downward I saw something like the appearance of fire, and there was brightness all around Him.

28Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on a day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. That was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard the voice of One speaking.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "in the thirtieth year… the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's exile" — two dates, and the first is not said to be of anything: the book never says what the thirtieth year counts from. The second is the exiles' own count, from the year the king was taken to Babylon (2 Kings 24:12–15). The prophet speaks as I in v1, and v3 names him in the third person, Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest.

  • v3 "the hand of the LORD was on him there" — Ezekiel's words for being seized by the LORD. The hand comes on him again at 3:14 and 3:22, each time before he is moved or shown something.

  • vv4, 27 "something like the gleam of amber" — chashmal, found only in Ezekiel (here, v27 and 8:2). What it names is not known. The Greek has ēlektron, its word both for amber and for a shining alloy of gold and silver. The English takes the first; either way it is something that glows in the fire.

  • vv5, 10 "four living creatures… the face of a human… a lion… an ox… an eagle" — chayyot, plain "living things." The book names them later: he sees them again by the river Chebar and knew that they were cherubim (10:20), and there the face of the ox is called the face of a cherub (10:14).

  • v14, v24 "darted back and forth… like the voice of the Almighty, a sound of tumult like the sound of an army" — the Greek has neither: no v14, and in v24 only like the sound of much water. Shaddai, the Almighty, appears here for the first time in the book.

  • v22 "the likeness of an expanse… spread out over their heads" — raqia, the word of the second day: Let there be a beaten expanse in the middle of the waters (Genesis 1:6). In Genesis it holds back the waters above; here it carries the throne.

  • v26 "something like the appearance of sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne" — what the elders saw at Sinai, under His feet was something like brickwork of sapphire (Exodus 24:10). Ezekiel sees the stone again, and now a throne on it.

  • v28 "Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on a day of rain" — the bow of the covenant with Noah, My bow I have set in the cloud (Genesis 9:13).

  • v28 "the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD" — the chapter piles up two words, mar'eh, "appearance," and demut, "likeness," more than twenty times, and never once says that Ezekiel saw the LORD. At the top of it all is the appearance of the likeness of the glory, three steps removed, and that is where he falls on his face.

chapters.title: Son of Man
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 2

1He said to me, "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."

2As He spoke to me, the spirit entered me and set me on my feet, and I heard Him speaking to me.

3He said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the sons of Israel, to rebellious nations that have rebelled against Me. They and their fathers have transgressed against Me to this very day.

4The sons are hard-faced and hard-hearted. I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.'

5As for them, whether they hear or refuse — for they are a rebellious house — they will know that a prophet has been among them.

6As for you, son of man, do not be afraid of them or afraid of their words, though briers and thorns are around you and you live among scorpions. Do not be afraid of their words or dismayed by their looks, for they are a rebellious house.

7You shall speak My words to them, whether they hear or refuse, for they are rebellious.

8But you, son of man, hear what I am saying to you: do not be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I am giving you."

9I looked: a hand was stretched out to me, and in it was a scroll.

10He spread it out before me, and it was written on the front and on the back; and written on it were laments and mourning and woe.

Notes

  • v1 "Son of man" — ben adam, "son of a human," a member of humankind. It is God's name for Ezekiel throughout the book, and it comes first just after the vision of a likeness like the appearance of a human on the throne (1:26). The one on the throne only looks like a human; the one on the ground is one.

  • v2 "the spirit entered me and set me on my feet" — ruach, with no of the LORD and no article: the word of the storm wind (1:4) and of the spirit that moved the living creatures and the wheels (1:12, 20). What drove the creatures now enters the man and stands him up. It lifts him again at 3:12 and 3:14.

  • v3 "to rebellious nations" — goyim, the word for the nations, said here of Israel. The rest of the chapter has a name for them, a rebellious house (vv5, 6, 8), and the book keeps it (3:9, 26, 27).

  • v4 "hard-faced and hard-hearted" — qeshei fanim ve-chizqei lev. The second word is the root of Ezekiel's own name, Yechezqel, "God makes strong," and 3:7–9 turns on it.

  • vv5, 7 "whether they hear or refuse" — the commission does not depend on being heard. Its only promised result is they will know that a prophet has been among them.

  • v6 "briers and thorns… scorpions" — sarabim, found only here, and sallonim, found again only at 28:24; both are taken as thorny plants from the context.

  • vv8–10 "eat what I am giving you… a scroll" — Jeremiah said, Your words were found, and I ate them (Jeremiah 15:16); for Ezekiel the eating is not a figure, and the next chapter tells it.

  • v10 "written on the front and on the back" — like the tablets at Sinai, written on both their sides, on one side and on the other (Exodus 32:15). Both sides are full, and all of it is laments and mourning and woe.

chapters.title: A Watchman for the House of Israel
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 3

1He said to me, "Son of man, eat what you find. Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel."

2So I opened my mouth, and He gave me this scroll to eat.

3He said to me, "Son of man, feed your belly and fill your stomach with this scroll that I am giving you." So I ate it, and in my mouth it was as sweet as honey.

4He said to me, "Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak My words to them.

5For you are not being sent to a people of speech too deep to understand and of heavy tongue, but to the house of Israel;

6not to many peoples of speech too deep to understand and of heavy tongue, whose words you cannot understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you.

7But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to Me; for all the house of Israel are hard-browed and hard-hearted.

8I have made your face as hard as their faces, and your brow as hard as their brows.

9Like diamond, harder than flint, I have made your brow. Do not be afraid of them or dismayed by their looks, for they are a rebellious house."

10He said to me, "Son of man, all My words that I speak to you, take into your heart and hear with your ears.

11Go to the exiles, to the sons of your people, and speak to them and say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says,' whether they hear or refuse."

12Then the spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great rumbling: "Blessed be the glory of the LORD from His place!"

13It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, the sound of a great rumbling.

14The spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went bitter, in the heat of my spirit, and the hand of the LORD was strong on me.

15I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, who lived by the river Chebar. I sat where they were sitting, and I sat there seven days among them, stunned.

The Watchman

16And it came to pass at the end of seven days that the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

17"Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. When you hear a word from My mouth, you shall warn them from Me.

18When I say to the wicked, 'You shall surely die,' and you do not warn him or speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way to save his life, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but his blood I will require from your hand.

19But if you warn the wicked, and he does not turn from his wickedness or from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity, but you will have saved your life.

20When a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does wrong, and I lay a stumbling block before him, he shall die. Because you did not warn him, he shall die in his sin, and the righteous deeds he has done shall not be remembered; but his blood I will require from your hand.

21But if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he shall surely live, because he took warning; and you will have saved your life."

Bound and Silent

22The hand of the LORD was on me there, and He said to me, "Get up, go out into the plain, and there I will speak with you."

23So I got up and went out into the plain, and the glory of the LORD was standing there, like the glory I had seen by the river Chebar; and I fell on my face.

24Then the spirit entered me and set me on my feet, and He spoke with me and said to me, "Go, shut yourself inside your house.

25As for you, son of man, they will put cords on you and bind you with them, so that you cannot go out among them.

26I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, and you will be mute and unable to rebuke them, for they are a rebellious house.

27But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.' Whoever will hear, let him hear; and whoever refuses, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house."

Notes

  • v3 "in my mouth it was as sweet as honey" — the words of the psalm, sweeter than honey to my mouth (Psalm 119:103), though the scroll was written with laments and mourning and woe (2:10). In v14 he goes away bitter.

  • vv5–6 "a people of speech too deep to understand and of heavy tongue" — imqei safah ve-khivdei lashon. Isaiah used the first for the foreign invader, the people of a speech too deep to understand (Isaiah 33:19); the second is Moses' word for himself, heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue (Exodus 4:10). Israel speaks Ezekiel's language, and that is the trouble: foreigners would have listened.

  • vv7–9, 14 "hard-browed… I have made your face as hard as their faces… the hand of the LORD was strong on me" — chazaq, "hard, strong," four times in three verses and again in v14: the root of Yechezqel, "God makes strong." The people are hard; God makes the prophet harder, like diamond, harder than flint. Shamir, "diamond," is Jeremiah's word for the point that writes Judah's sin, with a point of diamond it is engraved (Jeremiah 17:1).

  • vv12–13 "the sound of a great rumbling: 'Blessed be the glory of the LORD from His place!'" — ra'ash, the word for an earthquake. The Greek also reads Blessed. What he hears behind him is the vision of chapter 1 moving off: the wings of the living creatures and the wheels.

  • v15 "I sat there seven days among them, stunned" — mashmim, appalled, struck silent, as Job's friends sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him (Job 2:13).

  • vv17–21 "I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel" — tsofeh, the man on the wall who sees what is coming. God had said to Israel through Jeremiah, I set watchmen over you (Jeremiah 6:17); now one man is set, and his own life hangs on whether he gives warning. The charge is given again in the same words at 33:7–9.

  • v20 "I lay a stumbling block before him" — mikhshol, Jeremiah's word, I am about to lay stumbling blocks before this people (Jeremiah 6:21). The stumbling block is God's; the warning is the prophet's.

  • vv25–27 "they will put cords on you… you will be mute… But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth" — the prophet is bound and silent except when God speaks through him. The silence is lifted when word comes that the city has fallen (24:27; 33:22).

chapters.title: The Siege on a Brick
chapters.html:
Ezekiel 4

1"As for you, son of man, take a brick and set it before you, and engrave on it a city, Jerusalem.

2Lay siege against it: build a siege wall against it, heap up a ramp against it, set camps against it, and place battering rams against it all around.

3As for you, take an iron griddle and set it up as an iron wall between you and the city. Set your face toward it, and it will be under siege, and you shall besiege it. This is a sign for the house of Israel.

4As for you, lie on your left side and lay the guilt of the house of Israel on it. For the number of days that you lie on it, you shall carry their guilt.

5I have assigned you the years of their guilt as a number of days, three hundred and ninety days; so you shall carry the guilt of the house of Israel.

6When you have completed these, you shall lie a second time, on your right side, and carry the guilt of the house of Judah forty days, a day for each year, a day for each year; I have assigned it to you.

7You shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem with your arm bared, and you shall prophesy against it.

8I will put cords on you, so that you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have completed the days of your siege.

9As for you, take wheat and barley, beans and lentils, millet and spelt, put them in one vessel, and make bread of them for yourself. For the number of days that you lie on your side, three hundred and ninety days, you shall eat it.

10The food you eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day; you shall eat it at set times.

11You shall drink water by measure, a sixth of a hin; you shall drink it at set times.

12You shall eat it as a barley cake, baking it on human dung in their sight."

13The LORD said, "This is how the sons of Israel will eat their bread unclean among the nations where I will drive them."

14Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I have never been made unclean. From my youth until now I have never eaten an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts, and no foul meat has ever entered my mouth."

15He said to me, "See, I give you cow dung instead of human dung, and you shall prepare your bread on it."

16He said to me, "Son of man, I am about to break the staff of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight and in anxiety, and drink water by measure and in horror,

17so that they will lack bread and water, and look at one another in horror, and rot away in their guilt."

Notes

  • vv1–3 "take a brick… engrave on it a city, Jerusalem… an iron griddle… as an iron wall" — the prophet acts out the siege in miniature: a clay brick for the city, siege works around it, and an iron griddle set up as a wall between the prophet and the city. He is to set his face toward it, the face God has just made hard (3:8–9).

  • vv4–6 "three hundred and ninety days… forty days, a day for each year" — the sentence in the wilderness counted the other way: By the number of the days you scouted out the land, forty days — a year for each day — you shall carry your guilt forty years (Numbers 14:34). Here the years of guilt are lived out as days, and carry the guilt is the same phrase. The Greek has one hundred and ninety days in vv5 and 9.

  • v4 "lay the guilt of the house of Israel on it… you shall carry their guilt" — nasa avon, the law's phrase for bearing the guilt of a wrong (Leviticus 7:18; 17:16). The prophet carries the people's guilt in his own body, lying on one side for more than a year.

  • v8 "I will put cords on you" — the cords that the people will put on him (3:25), God now puts on him Himself.

  • vv9–11 "twenty shekels a day… a sixth of a hin" — starvation rations: bread of whatever grains are left, mixed in one jar, eaten by weight, and water by the measure. At set times, literally "from time to time": at fixed intervals, not when he is hungry.

  • v14 "Ah, Lord GOD! I have never been made unclean" — the cry Jeremiah made at his call, Ah, Lord GOD! I do not know how to speak (Jeremiah 1:6). The priest protests by the law he has kept: an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts (Leviticus 17:15), and piggul, foul meat (Leviticus 7:18). God gives way on the dung, not on the hunger.

  • vv16–17 "I am about to break the staff of bread… They will eat bread by weight… and rot away in their guilt" — the curse of the law, word for word: When I break your staff of bread, ten women will bake your bread in one oven and ration it out by weight (Leviticus 26:26), and they will rot away in their guilt (26:39).

speech.text: Ezekiel 4
"As for you, son of man, take a brick and set it before you, and engrave on it a city, Jerusalem.
Lay siege against it: build a siege wall against it, heap up a ramp against it, set camps against it, and place battering rams against it all around.

As for you, take an iron griddle and set it up as an iron wall between you and the city. Set your face toward it, and it will be under siege, and you shall besiege it. This is a sign for the house of Israel.
As for you, lie on your left side and lay the guilt of the house of Israel on it. For the number of days that you lie on it, you shall carry their guilt.
I have assigned you the years of their guilt as a number of days, three hundred and ninety days; so you shall carry the guilt of the house of Israel.

When you have completed these, you shall lie a second time, on your right side, and carry the guilt of the house of Judah forty days, a day for each year, a day for each year; I have assigned it to you.
You shall set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem with your arm bared, and you shall prophesy against it.
I will put cords on you, so that you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have completed the days of your siege.

As for you, take wheat and barley, beans and lentils, millet and spelt, put them in one vessel, and make bread of them for yourself. For the number of days that you lie on your side, three hundred and ninety days, you shall eat it.
The food you eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day; you shall eat it at set times.
You shall drink water by measure, a sixth of a hin; you shall drink it at set times.
You shall eat it as a barley cake, baking it on human dung in their sight."
The LORD said, "This is how the sons of Israel will eat their bread unclean among the nations where I will drive them."

Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I have never been made unclean. From my youth until now I have never eaten an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts, and no foul meat has ever entered my mouth."
He said to me, "See, I give you cow dung instead of human dung, and you shall prepare your bread on it."
He said to me, "Son of man, I am about to break the staff of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight and in anxiety, and drink water by measure and in horror,
so that they will lack bread and water, and look at one another in horror, and rot away in their guilt."
